display.purpose: The version on a boarding-pass card, fitted to the card width by container query. Release page h1 uses the same face at clamp(2rem, 7vw, 3.25rem), line-height 1.05.

headline.purpose: The home page h1 only. 1.5rem on mobile, 1.875rem from 640px. Sans, balanced.

title.purpose: The version at the top of the notes sheet.

band.purpose: Minor-version line name in a sticky board band.

data.purpose: Version links in rows and card field values. Row dates and ages use 13px at 400 in graphite.

body.purpose: Intro copy, footer, empty states, release notes prose. 0.875rem to 1rem; notes capped at 70ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase 11px mono label that names a data value: boarding-pass dt, column headers, band counts.

shadows.name: control
shadows.purpose: Outline buttons, search input group, channel toggle group (shadow-xs).

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Notes sheet and dropdown menu (shadow-lg). The sheet also sits on a 50% black scrim.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Control feedback (150ms color transitions, 0.97 press scale) and the 200ms notes fade-in. Overrides Tailwind's built-in ease-out.

motion.name: ease-drawer
motion.purpose: Notes sheet and scrim: 300ms in, 200ms out. Reduced motion falls back to a fade.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Declared for on-screen movement. No shipped component uses it yet.

narrative.overview:
Releases read like a gate board at an airport: a ranked, dense list of rows ordered by time, with every version and date set in tabular mono figures. The board sits on warm, near-neutral paper (hue 90, chroma under 0.01) with white panels and hairline rules. Nothing is decorated. Hierarchy comes from scale contrast alone: giant mono version numbers against small uppercase mono field labels.

Two boarding-pass cards lead the page, one for the latest stable and one for the latest canary. Each has the version fitted to the card width, a dashed perforation rule, and labeled segments (channel, published, age). Below them, a sticky search bar and channel toggle sit over a table that is split into sticky minor-version bands with release counts. Notes open in a right-hand sheet so the visitor never leaves the board. Each release also has its own page at `/releases/<tag>` that reuses the same display version, badges, and prose treatment in a narrower column.

There is exactly one hue in the system. Signal orange marks the newest published release and nothing else. Stable and canary are told apart by a filled versus outlined label, never by color. The site is unofficial, so it carries no Vercel or Next.js marks; the wordmark is just "Next.js Releases" set in Geist Mono.
keyCharacteristics: Warm off-white paper with white panels, both light and dark themes
Geist Mono for every version, date, count, and field label; Geist Sans for prose and controls
One alert hue (signal), used only on the Newest mark
Labeled segments and dashed perforation rules borrowed from boarding passes
Dense rows (6px vertical cell padding) with sticky minor-version bands
Flat surfaces, hairline borders, shadcn new-york primitives

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: The signal hue appears in exactly one component: the Newest mark on the single most recently published release. It never marks a channel, a link, a hover, a button, or a heading. If a second thing needs attention, it gets weight or scale, not signal.

rules.name: The Label Not Color Rule
rules.body: Stable is a filled ink badge, canary (and other pre-releases) an outlined badge. Both carry the channel name in text. Never encode channel by hue.

rules.name: The Mono For Machines Rule
rules.body: Anything a machine produced (a tag, a date, a count, a relative age) is Geist Mono with `tabular-nums slashed-zero`. Anything a person reads as a sentence is Geist Sans.

rules.name: The Scale Contrast Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from size jumps between display versions and 11px labels, not from color or extra weights. Only 400, 500, and 600 are used.

rules.name: The Labeled Segment Rule
rules.body: The 11px uppercase mono label only ever names a data value directly beneath or beside it (a `<dt>`, a column header, a count). It is never a floating eyebrow above a heading.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px hairline border or a tonal step. Sticky surfaces (search strip, bands) get a solid paper background so rows slide under them cleanly, never a blur or a shadow.

dos: Do set every version, date, count, and relative age in Geist Mono with `tabular-nums slashed-zero`.
Do keep the signal hue on the Newest mark only, and keep that mark on one release at a time.
Do tell channels apart with the filled Stable badge versus the outlined canary badge, always with the channel name in text.
Do label data segments with 11px uppercase mono labels in graphite, placed directly on the value they name.
Do separate surfaces with 1px hairlines and tonal steps, and give sticky strips a solid paper background.
Do use the motion tokens: `--ease-out` for control feedback (150ms) and content fades (200ms), `--ease-drawer` for the sheet (300ms in, 200ms out), with a reduced-motion fallback.
Do keep the OG hex copies in `src/lib/og/shared.tsx` in sync when a light-theme token changes.
donts: Don't use signal (or any new hue) for links, hover states, buttons, headings, or channel coding.
Don't use Vercel or Next.js logos or marks as the site's identity. The wordmark is the text "Next.js Releases" in Geist Mono.
Don't turn the uppercase mono label into an eyebrow or kicker above a heading. It only names a data value.
Don't add heavier shadows, glass, or blur to resting surfaces. Lift is reserved for overlays.
Don't add weights beyond 400, 500, and 600, or a third typeface.
